Tests exist in assembly.test.tsx, but they were not run during this reading.

terms.meaning: A saved description of one part in an assembly: its shape, size, position, rotation, material and how many times it repeats.
Where a value came from, such as measured source data, a typical assumption, or a manual edit.
A unit for angles used by the server. A full turn is about 6.28 radians, while the editor shows degrees, where a full turn is 360.
A working copy of the data where every number is text, so a partly typed value can be held without error.
The stand-in default used when no real parts exist for a component.
The total count of parts after each recipe's repeats are multiplied out.

used_by: Other frontend files that edit assemblies are not visible in this file.

sections.name: File setup, ASSEMBLY_AXES, RecipeVector
sections.title: Shared names for axes and value groups
sections.what: Declares the three directions and the four named groups of numbers used by a recipe: dimensions, local position, local rotation and repeat offset.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list of directions and names lets the checks loop over them the same way every time and catches typos.

sections.name: RecipeDraft
sections.title: Editable text form of a recipe
sections.what: Describes the editor's working copy of a recipe, where every number is held as text so that partly typed values can be kept.
sections.why: Likely reason: text lets the user type freely, and the values are only turned into numbers when checked.
sections.watch_out: Values stay as text until they are checked, so nothing here guarantees that a value is a number.

sections.name: recipeDraft
sections.title: Loading a saved recipe into the editor
sections.what: Turns a saved recipe into the text form the editor shows, changing rotations from radians into degrees for display.
sections.why: Likely reason: people read angles in degrees, so the editor shows degrees even though the server stores radians.
sections.watch_out: Rotations are shown in degrees, and saving converts them back to radians, so the two units must not be mixed.

sections.name: newRecipe
sections.title: Starting values for a new part
sections.what: Creates a new one-piece recipe, either a box or a cylinder, sized 1 in each direction, with no offset, repeated once, and the default material key.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond giving the editor a sensible blank part.

sections.name: initialRecipes
sections.title: Choosing the starting recipes
sections.what: Picks what the editor opens with: a saved assembly first, then existing parts converted into recipes with unique slot names, and otherwise one default box sized to the component, marked as a fallback.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fallback box is a rough stand-in, and marking it lets the screen tell users it is not detailed geometry.
sections.watch_out: If the fallback flag is lost, a rough box could be treated as real geometry by the user.

sections.name: validateRecipes, ParameterProvenance
sections.title: Checking all recipes before saving
sections.what: Checks the whole list before it goes to the server: 1 to 256 recipes, unique slot names of up to 128 characters, text limits, whole-number repeats from 1 to 256, at most 4,096 expanded parts, finite numbers within limits, and equal X and Z for cylinders. It converts rotations to radians and returns only the fields the server expects. It also declares the type used for labels.
sections.why: Likely reason: refusing bad input here gives a clear message on the page, instead of a failure after saving.
sections.watch_out: The limits are written here and must agree with the server, which is not visible in this file.

sections.name: parameterProvenance
sections.title: Deciding where each value came from
sections.what: Returns a label for one value: manual if the user changed it, if it was marked manual, or if an accepted recipe repeat; evidence if a source fact supports it; and default otherwise. Coarse geometry labels are used only when no finer label exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: users need to know which numbers are verified, and the comments explain that repeats on explicit parts should not inherit unrelated geometry labels.
sections.watch_out: The checks run in a fixed order, and changing that order changes many labels at once. A manual flag wins over evidence.

summary: Turns the assembly editor's part recipes into checked data for the server, and works out the label that shows where each value came from.
purpose: Lets a user build a component from parts, makes sure the recipes are valid before they are saved, and shows whether each value is manual, based on evidence, or a default.
why: Likely reason: the editor works with text while the user types, but the server needs numbers in a fixed shape. The checks and conversions are kept in one file so the rules stay consistent.
how: 1. Load stored recipes, or convert existing parts, or fall back to one default box (initialRecipes). 2. Show recipes as editable text (recipeDraft). 3. Start a new part with default values (newRecipe). 4. On save, check every recipe and convert it to the server shape (validateRecipes). 5. For each value, decide its label (parameterProvenance).
inputs: Component data from the model, including any stored assembly, existing parts and the material key. The user's typed text for each recipe. Which values the user edited by hand.
outputs: Starting recipes with a fallback flag. Text forms for editing. Checked recipes in the server shape, with rotations in radians. A label for each value.
risks: The validation limits must match the server, which is not visible in this file. A wrong label order would mislabel values. Degree and radian conversion is easy to get wrong if units differ.
debug: If saving says a recipe is invalid, the message names the recipe number and the reason, so check that field. If a label looks wrong, check the source links on the part and the order of checks in parameterProvenance. If starting parts look wrong, check initialRecipes.
